notes: This contract pins Umbra's opt-in, non-installable IEEE 1516.1-2025 resign-action slice to the exact C++ RTIambassador declaration exported by the Requirements Lab. The tests exercise the official action argument, ownership-precondition exceptions, unconditional divestiture/assumption delivery, delete-privileged object removal, a direct voluntary delete-then-divest transition, standalone cancellation and pending-acquisition rejection, cancellation of a negotiated-divestiture confirmation selected for the departing acquirer, cancellation of an If Available reservation and its stale requester callback, the final-federate directive-2 rule, bounded continuation of assumption search after later eligibility, and the final selected-file service report for a successful voluntary resignation. A matching timestamped object-deletion case keeps an accepted Remove Object Instance payload for two recipients after the producing owner resigns with UNCONDITIONALLY_DIVEST_ATTRIBUTES, then proves callback-before-grant delivery. The private registry regression also proves that an unavailable assumption callback route is rejected before any delete/divest mutation. A separate Connection Lost case now reaches the DELETE_OBJECTS action through the configured Automatic Resign Directive, and the distinct bounded Federate Resigned callback has its own contract. It is source/API traceability only: remaining automatic-resign combinations, complete forced-resign disposition policy, complete ownership arbitration, RTI-owned state, remote transport, packaging, JUnit evidence, protected review, and conformance remain open.
